intelligence.human_view: A view you cannot leave is a trap, not a page: the citizen clicked in to look, and the only way out was gone. The agreement is the front door's own story — the citizen must be able to read it and come back, read the other one and come back, and walk in when ready. The "‹ Login" control is the way back, and a way back that doesn't work is worse than no way back at all, because it promises and fails. The lesson is in the verb: verified. The control exists; what failed is that nobody checked it works. A back button is checked, not assumed — that is the difference between the law and the label.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you walk into a room to look at a beautiful picture, and when you turn around — the door is gone! You can't get back out! That's what happened here. So we make sure the door is always there, and we CHECK that it opens — from the picture room back to the hallway, and from the hallway back to the front door. No getting stuck!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — he went in to read the agreement, and when he wanted to come back, there was no way back. So we check the little "‹ Login" link properly — make sure it really takes you back, dear — from the pictures back to the beginning, and from the beginning back to the front page. No dead ends, anywhere.
intelligence.naya_view: Back from the agreement: the "‹ Login" control must be verified working. Back button covers the agreement views — deck → opening view, letter → opening view, opening view → front page. No dead ends anywhere.
